ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Bimodal distribution with a predominant low-intensity (black) central region and high-intensity (white) lateral fields. The ratio of low-intensity to high-intensity pixels is approximately 1.5:1.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous high-intensity regions occupy the distal thirds of both lobes. The central medial region is a solid low-intensity block. Transitional zones between intensity fields exhibit high-frequency mottling and isolated low-intensity spots within the white fields.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped indentation at the axial midline. The exact vertex angle is obscured by high-intensity water spray, but the converging edges suggest an acute angle.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous sequence of irregular serrations along the entire trailing edge. Serrations are more pronounced and frequent on the distal halves of each lobe compared to the medial edges.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Concave curvature along the superior trailing edge, terminating in tapered and slightly upturned distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Textured, high-contrast clusters localized at the extreme distal tips of both lobes. Multiple small punctate white marks are scattered across the dark central fluke surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Faint, dark linear disruptions are visible on the high-intensity field of the left lobe. A distinct, high-contrast circular ring-shaped mark is present on the right lobe's high-intensity field.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent circular ring-shaped scar on the right lobe white field. Significant textured encrustations (consistent with barnacle colonization) at the lobe tips.
other_distinctive_markers: A highly unique circular pigmentation ring on the right fluke lobe and a high density of water-droplet specular highlights across the lower central fluke surface.
